summary_paragraph: A 50-year-old woman with a history of common variable immunodeficiency, Hodgkin lymphoma, and recent allogeneic stem cell transplant was admitted for hypoglycemia and pleuritic chest pain. She was found to have MRSA pneumonia and bacteremia, with a mitral valve vegetation indicating endocarditis. She was treated with IV vancomycin and underwent port removal. She later developed VRE and Pseudomonas bacteremia, requiring daptomycin and ceftazidime. She had a prolonged course with neutropenia, managed with Neupogen, and required a PICC line for long-term antibiotics. Her lung infection improved over time, and repeat imaging showed resolving infiltrates. She was discharged home on a six-week course of vancomycin, heart failure medications, and optimized immunosuppressive and pulmonary regimens with close follow-up.
